title: Design key management and PKI as trust operations: concept decisions 2
teachingQuestion: Who controls the key or certificate transition, and what must a relying party validate?
focalInsight: PKI trust depends on protected issuance, an appropriate trust anchor, status, and complete relying-party validation.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Trust Anchor
nodes.definition: Configured root of trust accepted to validate an identity, certificate, or assertion.
nodes.detail: Configured root of trust accepted to validate an identity, certificate, or assertion.
nodes.decision: Select, protect, update, and constrain anchors under a trust policy.
nodes.failureExample: A device trusts a new root added by an unreviewed local administrator.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A trust anchor defines who can create accepted identity claims.

nodes.label: Certificate Validation
nodes.definition: Relying-party verification of chain, anchor, identity, time, purpose, constraints, and status.
nodes.detail: Relying-party verification of chain, anchor, identity, time, purpose, constraints, and status.
nodes.decision: Perform for the actual service or identity before accepting a secure channel or signature.
nodes.failureExample: A client ignores hostname mismatch and revocation information to restore availability.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Never convert a temporary validation bypass into a permanent trust rule.
